label: Hotel Allotments
purpose: Contracted hotel room allotments per hotel, room type, contract and stay night, with how much bookings have used and how much is still available. Use it for allotment, pickup and utilisation questions on upcoming stay nights.
grain: One allotment per hotel, room type and contract for each stay night; used rooms also carry the booking's date, customer and supplier.
use_for: total, used and available allotment by stay night, hotel, city, chain or room type
allotment utilisation by hotel or contract
allotment pickup by booking date, customer market or supplier
not_for: sales, cost, prices or profit (Sales Per Owned Hotels, Bookings)
booking or guest counts (Sales Per Owned Hotels, Bookings)
total or available allotment by customer, supplier or booking date

coverage.note: Stay nights from 2026-04 to 2027-12, mostly future nights: months far ahead have allotment but almost no usage yet. Booking dates of used allotment run from 2025-06 to 2026-10.

dates.label: Stay night (occupancy date)
dates.meaning: The night the allotment applies to (the cube's main date); includes future nights.

dates.label: Booking date
dates.meaning: When the booking that used the allotment was made; only [Used Allotment] has it (pickup analysis).

measures.name: [Total Allotment]
measures.label: Total allotment
measures.definition: Rooms contracted in allotment for each stay night; summed over several nights it gives room-nights.
measures.notes: Only breaks down by hotel-side attributes (stay night, hotel, city, country, chain, category, room type, contract, extranet, free sale): by customer it repeats the overall total and by booking date, supplier or cancellation it is blank (checked). Totals include very large allotments on extranet contracts (thousands of rooms per room type per night; 99% of all allotment), so utilisation is tiny overall; see review item hotel_allotments.utilisation_reliability.

measures.name: [Used Allotment]
measures.label: Used allotment
measures.definition: Rooms per stay night taken by non-cancelled bookings (free-sale bookings included).
measures.notes: Can be broken down by any attribute, including customer, market, supplier and booking date. About three quarters of it is free-sale inventory, which has no allotment.

measures.name: [Avail Allotment]
measures.label: Available allotment
measures.notes: Only breaks down by hotel-side attributes (stay night, hotel, city, country, chain, category, room type, contract, extranet, free sale): by customer it repeats the overall total and by booking date, supplier or cancellation it is blank (checked). Totals include very large allotments on extranet contracts (thousands of rooms per room type per night; 99% of all allotment), so utilisation is tiny overall; see review item hotel_allotments.utilisation_reliability.

measures.name: [% Used Allotment]
measures.label: Allotment utilisation
measures.definition: Used Allotment divided by Total Allotment.
measures.notes: Only breaks down by hotel-side attributes (stay night, hotel, city, country, chain, category, room type, contract, extranet, free sale): by customer it repeats the overall total and by booking date, supplier or cancellation it is blank (checked). Totals include very large allotments on extranet contracts (thousands of rooms per room type per night; 99% of all allotment), so utilisation is tiny overall; see review item hotel_allotments.utilisation_reliability.

measures.name: [% Avail Allotment]
measures.label: Allotment availability %
measures.definition: Available Allotment divided by Total Allotment.
measures.notes: Only breaks down by hotel-side attributes (stay night, hotel, city, country, chain, category, room type, contract, extranet, free sale): by customer it repeats the overall total and by booking date, supplier or cancellation it is blank (checked). Totals include very large allotments on extranet contracts (thousands of rooms per room type per night; 99% of all allotment), so utilisation is tiny overall; see review item hotel_allotments.utilisation_reliability.

rules: Total allotment, available allotment and both % measures only break down by hotel-side attributes (stay night, hotel, city, region, country, chain, category, room type, contract, extranet, free sale). By customer they repeat the overall total; by booking date, supplier or cancellation they are blank.
[Used Allotment] breaks down by anything, including customer, market, supplier and booking date.
Allotment summed over several stay nights is room-nights, not rooms; for 'rooms on a night' filter a single night.
Utilisation is tiny overall because extranet contracts carry very large allotments, and free-sale rooms count as used but have no allotment; say so when giving utilisation.
% measures are ratios: never add them across rows.
Always put a breakdown's needs_columns next to it; the Year and Month (number) columns need none.
Use the cube's measures only; never SUM a column.

examples.question: Total, used and available allotment for UAE hotels in December 2026
Allotment utilisation by hotel for stays next month
Allotment pickup by customer market for bookings made in September 2026

review.question: Total allotment holds very large values (thousands of rooms per room type per night, 99% on extranet contracts), so overall utilisation is about 0.1%. Should answers show utilisation as is, or limit it to non-extranet contracts?
options: Show as is, with a caveat
review.proposed: Show as is, with a caveat, and let the contracting team confirm which contracts hold real allotment
review.why: Non-extranet utilisation is also low (about 0.5%), so the filter does not fix the figure; hiding data would surprise users more than a stated caveat.
